gaps.explanation: Re-read p4 (Statement of Revenues, Expenditures, and Changes in Fund Balances - Cash Basis, Governmental Funds; printed p6) and the budget schedules p7 (General Fund, printed p17) and p8 (Special Fund, printed p18). Statement expenditure rows (Total column) 229,699 + 113,537 + 18,734 + 77,079 = 439,049; Transfers out 129,906 is printed on its own row (Special Revenue Fund column), and the column total 'Total other financing sources and uses' 568,955 includes it. Per fund: General Fund statement 202,215 + 113,537 + 18,734 + 77,079 = 411,565 = p7 'Operating expenses' 411,565 (detail[4]); Special Revenue Fund statement General government 27,484 vs p8 'Operating expenses' 157,390 (detail[7]) = 27,484 + Transfers out 129,906. The budget schedule prints the transfer inside its one operating-expenses line, with no transfer row. Schedule 411,565 + 157,390 = 568,955; statement 439,049; gap -129,906 = the transfer. No fund or row is missing and nothing is counted twice in detail (each fund appears once); the 157,390 is one printed amount and is kept as printed (no split, no derived 27,484 line). Difference is in the report itself.

p4 prints Transfers out 129,906 (Special Revenue Fund column). The Special Fund budget schedule p8 prints no transfer line: the 129,906 is inside its 'Operating expenses' 157,390 (detail[7], expenditure section). Adding a Transfers Out line from the statement would count the same 129,906 twice (rule: never add a line whose money is already inside an existing detail line). The General Fund side is in detail as 'Net transfers' 129,906 (p7, detail[3]) and matches transfers_in 129,906. This +129,906 and the expenditure -129,906 are the same money.
